title: B(e) NAMSE - Telemedicine-supported, interdisciplinary, and cross-age care for people with rare diseases through NAMSE-B center clusters
summary:
Chronically ill children, adolescents, and young adults with complex care needs in Germany frequently suffer from rare diseases, i.e., conditions affecting no more than 50 per 100,000 individuals. Care for affected individuals and their families is highly demanding and resource-intensive. There is a lack of interprofessional, sustainable, and reliable outpatient care that takes into account patients’ individuality, coordinates care processes, and also addresses issues beyond disease symptoms, such as health-promoting lifestyles, health literacy, and the mental health of both patients and their families.

This is where the new form of care B(e) NAMSE comes in, aiming to improve care for young people with rare diseases. The new form of care B(e) NAMSE is an add-on to standard care.
If a patient has a need for the new form of care B(e) NAMSE, a multidisciplinary team conducts a case conference after the initial assessment of the complex health condition. During this conference, existing patient records are reviewed and, if necessary, additional medical records are requested in order to develop an individual diagnostic and treatment plan. This process includes an exchange with the patient and, where applicable, with parents or legal guardians via videoconference.
Within the new form of care B(e) NAMSE, an online family training and health-related advance care planning are provided as needed. In addition, individualized, patient‑tailored training sessions are offered, focusing on issues beyond disease symptoms, such as health‑promoting lifestyles, health literacy, and mental health. These sessions are complemented by an educational website that provides both disease‑generic and disease‑specific information. For patients aged 15 years and above, a structured transition from pediatric and adolescent care to adult medicine is addressed.

The effectiveness of the new form of care B(e) NAMSE is evaluated in comparison with a waiting-list control group. While the intervention group receives the new form of care B(e) NAMSE immediately after randomization, the waiting-list group is initially managed within standard care for the first 6 months. After this period, patients in the waiting-list group also receive the new form of care. Thus, all participants included in the study eventually receive the intervention.

To assess the effectiveness of the new form of care B(e) NAMSE, up to five online surveys are conducted throughout the project at 6‑month intervals. These surveys include questionnaires on quality of care processes, symptom burden, dental care, physical activity, nutrition, sleep, quality of life, mental health, disease coping, health literacy, transition to adult care, use of health care services, and indirect disease‑related costs. For patients insured by one of the health and long-term care insurances participating in the project, routine data are additionally analyzed to evaluate the costs of the new form of care B(e) NAMSE, provided that a separate consent for the use of these data is available. In total, 1000 patients with a concrete suspected or confirmed diagnosis of a rare disease will be recruited.

In the qualitative part of the study, interviews with individual patients, parents/legal guardians, and healthcare providers will be conducted to examine in detail how the new form of care B(e) NAMSE is implemented. Interviews with patients and parents/legal guardians will be carried out 4 to 6 months after the individual start of the new form of care. Interviews with healthcare providers will be carried out 6, 12, and 18 months after the start of the new form of care at the respective study site. The interviews will also capture problems that arose during implementation, to improve the future implementation of the new form of care. At the end of the project, additional workshops will be held with healthcare providers from all participating centers. In these workshops, a manual/guideline with proposed solutions for implementation challenges will be developed.
conditions: Rare neurological diseases, rare neuromuscular diseases, rare pain disorders, rare gastroenterological diseases, rare dermatological diseases, rare cardiac diseases, rare renal diseases, rare cancer-predisposing syndromes, rare respiratory diseases, rare bone diseases, rare craniofacial malformations, rare genetic inner ear disorders, Klinefelter syndrome and variants, rare endocrine diseases, rare rheumatic diseases, rare immunodeficiencies, rare autoinflammatory diseases, rare autoimmune diseases and other rare diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria for the efficacy study of the new form of care B(e) NAMSE:
-No previous inclusion in the ongoing study
-Age between 0 and 25 years
-Statutory health insurance
-Rare disease (concrete suspected or confirmed diagnosis)
-Sufficient understanding of the German language
-Need for secondary and tertiary prevention
-Informed consent to participate in the efficacy study

Additional inclusion criteria for the routine data analysis:
-Insured with one of the participating health insurances
-Informed consent to participate in the routine data analysis
Exclusion criteria:
-Withdrawal of informed consent to participate in the efficacy study
-Death of the patient

Additional exclusion criterion for the routine data analysis:
-Withdrawal of informed consent to participate in the routine data analysis
